title: Hazel and the Thorn
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish, mercenary Lena Amberdale learns her silent god, Vess, was the ward's anchor—and that the theocracy that silenced him intends to remake the country as a godless prison-state. Hunted by her former order and guided by a smuggler's found family she never meant to love, Lena follows a dying priest's map toward the Door, the last exit from a nation being erased. At the Door she must choose: walk free alone or pour her sworn oath back into Vess to reignite the wards, knowing it will cost her memory of everyone she loves. She pays the price; Thornfell endures the winter, and her family remembers for her.
about_author: Yara Fairweather is the pen name of a former mountain guide who traded trail maps for story maps after a winter stranded in a fire lookout. They write fantasy about people who survive by belonging to each other rather than to institutions.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Guiding a cargo run through the Thornfell passes, Lena watches the stars extinguish one by one and feels her god's silence turn physical—the oath-scar on her wrist goes cold. Emotional beat: dread beneath professional calm, the moment invisibility dies.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Luck
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She reaches the waystation town of Cinderhollow and finds the border wards fallen: soldiers of the Radiant Concord pouring through, conscripting townsfolk. She saves a boy, Pip, from a press-gang on instinct. Beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Silence Cost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, flashback-woven. In hiding, she recalls how Vess went quiet seven years ago and how she built a life of small illegal kindnesses since. The Concord posts her name on execution writs—her old commander signed it. Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa, a mapmaker whose father charted the legendary Door out of Thornfell, bargains with Lena: safe routes in exchange for an escort to her father's hidden archive. Beat: wary alliance between two women who trust no institutions.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The party—Lena, Sefa, Pip, and disgraced Concord deserter Brannoc—travels roads only smugglers know while the Concord burns bridges behind them. First ambush survived together. Beat: found family forming under fire.

chapters.title: Cinders in the Snow
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. He confesses he helped design the ward-collapse ritual before defecting, revealing the Concord's Grand Inquisitor needs a living oath-bearer to finish silencing every god in the mountains. Beat: guilt offered as currency; the group must decide if he's worth trusting.

chapters.title: The Hollow Shrine
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They shelter in a shrine of Vess, desecrated but not dead—Lena hears a heartbeat in the stone. A dying priest gives her half a map to the Door and warns: 'A door opens both ways.' Beat: hope rekindled, ominous price foreshadowed.

chapters.title: Wolves of the Concord
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Inquisitor's elite hunters corner them at a river crossing; Pip is taken. Sefa chooses to burn her father's duplicate maps to cover their escape. Beat: rage and helplessness; the cost of being hunted.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Snow closes the high passes early—a magically induced winter meant to starve resistance. The group shelters with a village of ward-touched outcasts who feed them and ask nothing. Beat: warmth as rebellion; Lena almost stays.

chapters.title: Oath-Bearer
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. He explains the ritual fully: Vess wasn't silenced—he poured himself into his last sworn servant to hide. Lena is the anchor. The Concord doesn't want her dead; they want her opened. Beat: identity shattered—she is the weapon and the prize.

chapters.title: Pip's Winter
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Imprisoned in Cinderhollow, Pip befriends a jaded Concord clerk and steals the location of the Inquisitor's ritual site—which is also where they're keeping the Door's key-stone. Beat: small courage mattering; the child becomes the plot's hinge.

chapters.title: The Devil You Swore To
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In dreams, Vess finally speaks: fragmented, starving, ashamed. He offers her a truth and a choice but refuses to choose for her. Beat: intimacy with the divine; anger at a god who made her a hiding place without consent.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Glass Bridge
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Crossing a frozen gorge, they're ambushed by hunters led by Lena's former commander, Maren. Brannoc takes a mortal wound buying time. Beat: betrayal's face is someone Lena loved; grief hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: Ashes and Promises
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Brannoc dies asking Lena to finish what he broke. Sefa finds the second half of the Door-map sewn into her father's coat lining—the two halves align. Beat: mourning fused with momentum; the route is complete.

chapters.title: The Godless City
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Rescued during a prisoner transfer gone wrong, Pip guides the group through Cinderhollow's tunnels as the city rises in spontaneous revolt against the Concord. Beat: ordinary people choosing each other over fear; the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confronts Maren alone and learns the Concord promised to restore their dead god too—they are sisters in grief, weaponized differently. Lena refuses to kill her. Beat: mercy as defiance; the antagonist humanized.

chapters.title: The Ritual Site
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The group infiltrates the Door's antechamber as the Inquisitor begins the final unmaking, using captured oath-bearers as fuel. Pip's stolen knowledge gets them past the wards. Beat: ticking-clock tension; everything converges.

chapters.title: Open the Bearer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Captured, Lena is strapped into the extraction rite; the Inquisitor peels at Vess inside her. Memories of her family begin tearing loose. Beat: body-horror anguish; the lowest point—she nearly lets go just to stop the pain.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Thornfell
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Sefa, Pip, and the revolt breach the chamber; Maren, seeing the Inquisitor torture children of the ward-touched, turns her blade against her own order. The Door stands open—free passage out. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the choice made real.

chapters.title: What Lena Amberdale Chose
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Instead of fleeing, Lena walks backward through the threshold and pours her entire oath—every memory of Sefa, Pip, Brannoc, the road—into Vess. The wards reignite; the stars return; the winter breaks. Beat: triumphant devastation; climax resolved through sacrifice, not violence.

chapters.title: Spring, Remembering
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Weeks later, a stranger with Lena's eyes and empty hands walks into Cinderhollow. Sefa and Pip begin telling her their stories, refusing to let the sacrifice erase the person. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; found family repaying its debt.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, fragmented then whole. Among returned memories is a name she'd forgotten she carried—Hazel, the girl she was before the oath. She plants a hazel sapling over Vess's restored shrine and signs the smugglers' ledger with her true name. Beat: wholeness reclaimed; justice lived outside the law, power given away freely.
